description: The value one site/data/series-<code>.js file assigns to window.__<prefix>SeriesReg['<num>'] (prefix is per-repo, e.g. __ffSeriesReg -- out of scope for a schema, which only covers the assigned object literal). `num` should match an entry in this repo's own index.js SERIES_ORDER (schema: index.schema.json) -- a cross-file constraint this single-file schema can't enforce itself.

num.description: Short code, e.g. 'I'..'XVI', 'MQ', 'SW', 'CC', 'DFF', 'DM', 'TR', 'EX', 'BE', 'WD', 'PB', 'FAN', 'Other', 'AN' -- per-repo, not a fixed enum.

url.description: Series-level wiki link. Omit or null for an unlinked heading.

note.description: Prose blurb under the heading. May contain literal '\n\n'-separated paragraphs.

notePartsMap.description: Maps an exact `note` string (or one of its '\n\n'-split paragraphs) to a DescPart[] run for inline <em>/<abbr> styling -- keyed by literal text match, not an index.

chronoOrder.description: Series sort key for Chronological mode. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

recommendedOrder.description: Series sort key for Narrative mode (the default). Defaults to 0 when omitted.

releaseDate.description: Present in real data but not read anywhere in the current page.dc.html -- vestigial; kept optional so existing data stays valid.

DateValue.description: title_date / subtitle_date. A plain year, a full date optionally carrying a two-digit same-day tie-break ord suffix (' 10' / ' 20'), or a {start,end} range for the handful of multi-year pseudo-entries (`end` may be an open-ended '<year>+').

DescPart.description: One run inside a description[i] inner array (rendered by DescRun.dc.html). A bare string auto-wraps to {text}.

tip.description: Tooltip text. Required alongside tipText/hintText; optional alongside text/emText (e.g. { emText: ' (EU)', tip: 'Europe', helpStyle: 'cursor: help;' }).

jpTag.description: Appends ' (JP)'. Unrelated to a PlatformItem's own jpTag field.

helpStyle.description: Extra inline CSS on the wrapping span, e.g. 'cursor: help;'.

BylinePart.description: bylineParts[] item -- EntryByline.dc.html's own narrower shape, not the same object as DescPart.

label.description: Prefixes this segment, e.g. an FFXI expansion name.

tip.description: Tooltip, e.g. 'Main Story' / 'Main + Extra' / 'Completionist', or a custom tip like 'Solo' / 'Co-op' / 'Vs.'.

value.description: A code from catalogs.js's LANGUAGE_NAMES, or the literal '…?' sentinel.

native.description: Marks the original/source language. Not read by any component -- annotation only, kept for real data compatibility.

voice.description: Full audio/voiced. Mutually exclusive with textOnly in practice.

tip.description: Explicit tooltip override, used verbatim with no auto ' — full audio'/' — text only' suffix.

key.description: Looked up in platform-icons.js's PLATFORM_ICONS to merge in iconImg/iconSize/imgStyle/jpTag/base name.

url.description: This release's own link. On a top-level games[] entry, unset falls back to the row's platformsUrl; on an extras[]/alt/alts[] sub-entry it does not.

name.description: Full override of the displayed label, bypassing the catalog base-label + paren composition.

paren.description: Appends " (<paren>)" to the catalog's base label. Mutually exclusive with `name` in practice (name wins if both given).

terminated.description: Dims + strikes through the icon (service/store shut down).

noUrl.description: Common in real data alongside a null/absent url, but not read by any current template -- authoring annotation only.

prefix.description: Short text prefix before the icon (unlinked-icon render path), e.g. 'U' for an UltraHD Blu-ray variant.

icon.description: Bootstrap Icons class, alternative to iconImg.

text.description: Plain text badge instead of an icon.

ytSearch.description: Computes url as a YouTube search instead of a literal URL.

ytTitle.description: Overrides the search title. Near-universal alongside ytSearch -- default search results are poor without it.

ytSuffix.description: Overrides the appended suffix word(s) (default per key, e.g. fan-movie -> 'game movie'). Set to '' to suppress it.

pointerEvents.description: Observed once in real data; not read by any current component -- likely dead cruft, kept for real-data compatibility.

kind.description: Looked up in catalogs.js's RATING_KINDS (score-mode entries: {label}) or special-cased 'steam' (score is a STEAM_REVIEW_LABELS abbreviation).

label.description: Explicit tooltip text, overriding the `kind` catalog lookup -- the escape hatch for a rating source with no RATING_KINDS entry at all.

Rating.description: Either absent, or exactly one of two modes. A bare {score,url} with neither `scores`, `textOnly`, nor a badge-implying `kind` renders as nothing -- not a valid third shape.

oneOf.description: Score-link mode: one or more independently-resolved scores, no fixed critic/user slots.
Badge mode: a bare text/abbr score, no link-per-score.

kind.description: Catalog kind implying textOnly (e.g. 'nyr', 'tbd') and supplying abbrTerm/abbrDef.

score.description: Rendered as plain text -- not linked, even if `url` is also set.

SeriesEntry.description: One item in games[], and recursively the same shape for extras[] items, alts[] items, and the singular alt object. A sub-entry with no own title/subtitle inherits title/title_url/title_date/title_tip/title_italic wholesale from its immediate parent (all-or-nothing) -- not enforceable in this single-node schema.

id.description: Manual override of the derived slug/anchor id. Currently unused in real data but a valid escape hatch.

label.description: Deprecated/legacy freeform display text, paired with `url`. Still rendered ahead of the title/subtitle output when present -- prefer title/subtitle for new entries.

url.description: Deprecated/legacy link paired with `label`. Distinct from platformsUrl/storeUrl.

chronoOrder.description: Per-entry sort key for Chronological mode (mode B), read as `g.chronoOrder ?? 0`. Distinct from the series-level chronoOrder on the enclosing SeriesFile.

recommendedOrder.description: Per-entry sort key for Narrative mode (the default), read as `g.recommendedOrder ?? 0`. Distinct from the series-level recommendedOrder on the enclosing SeriesFile.

mainline.description: Counted for the intro's mainlineCount stat.

tags.description: Free-text byline words (joined with ' · ' unless bylineParts is set). 'Expansion' and 'DLC' reclassify a Game for stats-counting; 'Optional' excludes a game from the release-order pseudo-series' earliest-date computation. Everything else is display text only -- do not enum-restrict.

bylineParts.description: Alternative to a tags-derived byline, for an inline <abbr> in the byline. Wins over tags for display; tags are still read for their 'Expansion'/'DLC'/'Optional' semantics even when this is set.

platformGroups.description: Array of groups -- each inner array is a cluster of same-slot compatible platforms rendered together; each outer entry is one flex-wrapped icon position.

platforms.description: Legacy flat-array alias for platformGroups (not grouped). Not seen in current real data; kept for compatibility.

platformsUrl.description: Fallback URL for any platformGroups item lacking its own url. Only consumed on top-level games[] entries.

storeUrl.description: "Profile ↗" link next to the Platforms label header. Valid independently at games[]/extras[]/alt level.

langOrder.description: Per-entry override of the default language sort-priority order (default ['JA','EN']).

description.description: A bare string (one paragraph), or an array where each item is a plain string (one paragraph) or a nested DescPart[] run (one paragraph built from styled parts).

extras.description: "Other versions and platforms" toggle list under this row (or under alt / an alts[] item -- one level of nesting deep in practice).

alt.description: The singular "or <other version>" row rendered inline (not behind a toggle). May itself carry its own extras[].

alts.description: Plural parallel "or" rows (e.g. several unrelated adaptations of a book) -- distinct from the singular `alt`. Rare.

listTitle.description: FFXI-style linked heading rendered as a plain <ul> under the description, alongside listItems.

listItems.description: Plain strings only, no parts support.
